recommendations.title: Keep the oldfs filesystem driver from loading

cis_controls.title: Turn off what an asset does not use
Expose only the services a host needs

recommendations.description: `oldfs` reads a disk format that Synthetic Linux stopped writing three releases ago.
recommendations.rationale: Driver code for a format nobody uses can still be reached by plugging in a crafted disk. A driver that cannot load cannot be attacked that way.
recommendations.impact: Disks in the old format stop mounting on this host. Copy their data off first.
recommendations.audit:
Ask the module manager for the driver's state:

```
$ synthctl module status oldfs
oldfs: blocked, not loaded
$ synthctl module list --loaded | grep -c '^oldfs\b'
0
```

Any state other than `blocked` means the driver can still load.
recommendations.remediation:
Block the driver and take it out of the running kernel:

```
$ synthctl module block oldfs
$ synthctl module unload oldfs
```

recommendations.title: Require signed packages from every software source

cis_controls.title: Patch operating systems on a schedule

recommendations.description: `synthpkg` checks each package against the keys it trusts, unless a source's own file turns the check off.
recommendations.rationale: Without the check, whoever answers at a source's address decides what gets installed.
recommendations.audit:
Read the global value, then look for sources that override it:

```
$ synthpkg config get verify-signatures
true
$ grep -rlE 'verify-signatures[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*false' /etc/synth/sources.d/
```

The second command lists no files.
recommendations.remediation: Run `synthpkg config set verify-signatures true` and delete the `verify-signatures = false` line from each file the audit listed.
recommendations.references:
1. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: SI-7 - [https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)
2. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-14 - [https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)

recommendations.title: Run exactly one clock synchronization service

cis_controls.title: Keep every clock on one source

recommendations.description: Synthetic Linux ships two clock services, `synthclock` and `tickd`. Either keeps the system clock near a reference server.
recommendations.rationale: Events from several hosts can be lined up only if their clocks agree, and sign-in tickets are refused when clocks drift apart.
recommendations.audit:
```
$ synthctl service state synthclock tickd
synthclock: enabled, running
tickd: disabled, stopped
```

One service is enabled and running; the other is neither.
recommendations.remediation:
Pick one:

- **synthclock:** `synthctl service enable --now synthclock` and `synthctl service disable --now tickd`
- **tickd:** the same two commands with the names swapped
recommendations.additional_info: Only one time service should run: two services fight over the clock.

recommendations.title: Stop the host from routing packets between interfaces
recommendations.description: With `routing.ipv4` or `routing.ipv6` on, the kernel hands packets that arrive on one interface to another.
recommendations.rationale: A host that is not meant to be a router should not act as one: routing carries traffic past the boundary a firewall was put there to hold.
recommendations.impact: Hosts that carry traffic for containers or virtual machines need routing. Leave those out.
recommendations.audit:
```
$ synthctl net get routing.ipv4 routing.ipv6
routing.ipv4 = off
routing.ipv6 = off
```
recommendations.additional_info: Hosts running containers, virtual machines or VPN gateways are the usual exceptions.
recommendations.references:
1. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: SC-7 - [https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)
2. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-6 - [https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)

recommendations.title: Install the synthwall packet filter

cis_controls.title: Filter traffic at each end-user device

recommendations.description: `synthwall` decides in the kernel which packets reach which services.
recommendations.rationale: With no filter, every listening service answers every network the host is on.

recommendations.title: Set the synthwall incoming policy to discard

cis_controls.title: Filter traffic at each end-user device

recommendations.description: The incoming policy is what `synthwall` does with a packet after every rule has passed on it.
recommendations.rationale: With `discard`, the rules are a list of what is allowed, and a new service stays unreachable until someone adds one.
recommendations.impact: **Note:** change the policy at the console. A wrong rule order can drop the SSH session you are using.
recommendations.audit:
Read the policy and the rules above it:

```
$ synthwall show incoming
policy: discard
rule 1: allow loopback
rule 2: allow replies
```

Ask the host's owner whether each `[allow]` rule is still needed.
recommendations.remediation:
Allow loopback and replies first, then change the policy:

```
$ synthwall rule add incoming allow loopback
$ synthwall rule add incoming allow replies
$ synthwall policy incoming discard
```

recommendations.title: Limit who can change the SSH server configuration file
recommendations.description: `/etc/synth/ssh/server.conf`, and every file it pulls in, sets who may sign in over SSH.
recommendations.rationale: Whoever can edit the file can give themselves a way in.
recommendations.audit:
```
$ synthctl file mode /etc/synth/ssh/server.conf /etc/synth/ssh/server.d/*
/etc/synth/ssh/server.conf: 600 root:root
```

Every file shows `600` or less and `root:root`.
recommendations.references:
1. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AC-3 - [https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)
2. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: MP-2 - [https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)

recommendations.title: Allow no more than four sign-in attempts per SSH connection
recommendations.description: `auth-attempts` caps the passwords one connection may try. The server logs a connection once half of them have failed.
recommendations.rationale: A small cap makes guessing over one connection slow and puts failures in the log early.
recommendations.remediation: Put `auth-attempts 4` near the top of `/etc/synth/ssh/server.conf`, before any per-user section, and run `synthctl service reload ssh-server`.

recommendations.title: Show a warning notice before SSH sign-in
recommendations.description: `notice-file` names the text the server sends before asking for credentials.
recommendations.rationale: Some legal processes need users to have been told that the system is monitored.
recommendations.audit:
```
$ synthctl ssh effective-config | grep -E '^notice-file[[:space:]]+/'
notice-file /etc/synth/notice
```

The notice must not name the release: leave out the `\R` and `\K` substitutions.
recommendations.remediation: Set `notice-file /etc/synth/notice` in `/etc/synth/ssh/server.conf` and write the site's wording into that file.
recommendations.additional_info: The wording is for the site's legal staff to choose.

recommendations.title: Turn off graphical session forwarding over SSH

cis_controls.title: Turn off what an asset does not use

recommendations.description: `display-forwarding` carries a graphical session back to the client.
recommendations.rationale: Servers seldom need it, and it opens a path to the client's screen.
recommendations.audit:
```
$ synthctl ssh effective-config | grep display-forwarding
display-forwarding no
```

recommendations.title: Install the synthaudit event recorder
recommendations.description: `synthaudit` copies the kernel's event records to disk.
recommendations.rationale: Without it, the records of who changed what disappear once the kernel's buffer wraps.
recommendations.audit:
```
$ synthpkg query synthaudit synthaudit-rules
synthaudit <version> installed
synthaudit-rules <version> installed
```
recommendations.references:
1. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AU-2 - [https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)
2. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AU-12 - [https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)

recommendations.title: Keep full synthaudit logs instead of rotating them away
recommendations.description: `when-full` tells `synthaudit` what to do once a log reaches its size limit.
recommendations.rationale: Rotating a full log away throws out the records an investigation will ask for.
recommendations.impact: The logs keep growing until the disk is full, so send them to a collector and watch the space.
recommendations.audit:
```
$ synthctl audit config get when-full
when-full = keep
```
recommendations.remediation: Run `synthctl audit config set when-full keep`.
recommendations.additional_info: `warn-at` and `stop-at` decide what happens as the disk fills up.
recommendations.references:
1. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AU-4 - [https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)
2. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AU-11 - [https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)
